title: FlexStep: Enabling Flexible Error Detection in Multi/Many-core Real-time Systems
problem: Traditional error detection (e.g., LockStep) requires pre-configured checker cores and static regions, causing over-provisioning and reducing real-time performance in systems with mixed reliability requirements.
motivation: Safety-critical real-time systems need flexible resource allocation between reliability and performance; rigid error detection reduces schedulability.
method: FlexStep integrates hardware microarchitecture supporting dynamic core reconfiguration with OS scheduling layer; enables asynchronous, preemptive error detection via lightweight hardware support and OS-level task scheduling policies.
key_novelty: First systematic hardware-software co-design enabling flexible, dynamic error detection adapted to per-task reliability needs.
contributions: Dynamic core configuration and asynchronous error detection
Flexible task scheduling with heterogeneous reliability requirements
Improved resource efficiency and real-time schedulability
primary_theme: Flexible hardware-software error detection for real-time systems
